# s301 — add --id refuses an id a sibling worktree already filed

`slicer add --id X` refuses before writing when a sibling checkout's index already holds X as an item that did not come from the shared merge base, so two checkouts cannot file different items under one id.

**Findings:** nested-relay trial 2026-10-15: add --id s296 on the s294 branch collided with an uncommitted s296 on main; check warned only after the write · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-15** — add --id refuses an id a sibling worktree filed (id_taken_elsewhere, exit 2, nothing written); inherited-id logic lifted to verify.inherited_ids; import and promote need no change because outlines carry no id; full suite 2159 OK; review and gate PASS.

(2) case-fold: a sibling's s10 against our S10 is not refused (Index.get is case-sensitive, model.py:659-663); candidate for a new item. (3) migrate --force keeps explicit legacy ids; plausible sibling collision path, unchecked. (4) Spec premise: import and promote take no explicit id (outline.py:41 KEYS has no id; promote files no new id), so neither changed and test_Import_ExplicitIdFiledInSibling_RefusesWholeFile was not written.

## Why

In the nested-relay trial on 2026-10-15, the outer session filed a follow-up as `add --id s296` on the s294 branch. The main checkout had already filed a different s296 there, uncommitted ("Print the nested relay..."). `add` wrote it. Only the following `slicer check` warned "the two will collide on merge" (`check._sibling_collisions`, `src/slicer/check.py:70`). Undoing it took a revert commit and a re-file as s297.

The cause: `ids.allocate` (`src/slicer/ids.py:127`) checks an explicit id against this checkout's index only. The sibling floor (`cli._id_floor`, `src/slicer/cli.py:1049`) applies only to ids slicer picks itself. Leaving out `--id` would have avoided it, because `next-id` and the default allocation already respect sibling worktrees.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ops.py` / `src/slicer/ids.py`:
  - With an explicit id, refuse when a sibling checkout (`store.sibling_checkouts`) has that id and it is not in the index at the merge base. Reuse the inherited-id logic that `check._sibling_collisions` uses, lifted where both can call it.
  - Nothing is written.
  - Use a new stable code `id_taken_elsewhere` (exit 2). The message names the sibling worktree and its title for the id, and suggests `slicer next-id` or leaving out `--id`.
  - An id that both checkouts inherited, and outside a git repo, behave as today.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `add`. Also `import` and `promote` wherever an explicit id is taken from an outline, so all three refuse the same way.

- `tests/test_ids.py` or `tests/test_cli.py`, next to the existing sibling-worktree tests (use `support.isolated_discovery` for the fixture).
